title: The étale derived category is generated by finite-Tor constructible objects
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite admissible ring and $X$ in the standing range: the base field is $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $A$ is a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, and $X$ is of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sf-setting], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $\mathcal T=\D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ for the bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] of finite Tor amplitude: there exist integers $a\le b$ such that, for every sheaf $N$ of $A$-modules in degree zero, $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L N)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude], [def-kun-derived-tensor]. For any class $\mathcal S$ of objects of $\mathcal T$, $\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathcal T}(\mathcal S)$ denotes the intersection of the full replete triangulated subcategories [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] containing $\mathcal S$ and closed under arbitrary small coproducts in $\mathcal T$, with the fixed universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Then
$$\D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)=\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathcal T}(\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)).$$

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-etale-finite-ring-compact-generators] with $T=X$ and $C=A$. Its hypotheses hold because $k$ is algebraically closed, $X/k$ is finite type, and $A$ is finite and annihilated by a power of the invertible prime $\ell$. It gives a set $S$, in the fixed indexing universe, of objects $E_s\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ whose shifts detect isomorphisms. It also supplies arbitrary set-indexed coproducts and locally small Hom spaces for $\mathcal T$. Compactness of each $E_s$ follows from the blueprint's étale compactness theorem [det-ctf-finite-compact-etale], applied with the same $A$ and $X$.

source.place: Section 6.4, Example 6.4.1 and Proposition 6.4.8, printed pp. 48–49; the existing finite-ring compact-generator statement

proof.text: The family $(E_s)$ generates $\mathcal T$ in the precise sense of [def-pc-generators]. Indeed, suppose $\operatorname{Hom}(E_s[n],K)=0$ for every $s,n$. The map $0\to K$ induces bijections from these shifted objects, so the detection clause of [lem-pur-etale-finite-ring-compact-generators] gives $K\simeq0$. Equivalently, if $K$ is nonzero, there are $s,n$ and a nonzero map $E_s\to K[-n]$, by applying the inverse shift to a nonzero map $E_s[n]\to K$. The coproduct universal property extends that map to $\bigoplus_{t\in S}E_t\to K[-n]$ by using zero on the other summands; it stays nonzero because its restriction to summand $s$ is nonzero. Thus $\bigoplus_sE_s$ is a weak generator.

For any $K\in\mathcal T$, apply [lem-pc-compact-generators-build-objects] to the compact generating family of Steps 1–2. It provides objects $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ and triangles $Z_n\to X_n\to X_{n+1}\to Z_n[1]$, where $X_1$ and every $Z_n$ are coproducts of shifts of the $E_s$, together with a distinguished telescope triangle $\bigoplus_nX_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\bigoplus_nX_n\to K\to(\bigoplus_nX_n)[1]$. All the hypotheses of that statement are supplied above: $\mathcal T$ is triangulated, has the required coproducts, each $E_s$ is compact, and their coproduct is a weak generator.

Let $\mathcal L$ be any full replete triangulated subcategory of $\mathcal T$ closed under small coproducts and containing $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. Since it contains every $E_s$, shift closure and coproduct closure put $X_1$ and every $Z_n$ from Step 3 in $\mathcal L$. Inductively, the triangle $Z_n\to X_n\to X_{n+1}\to Z_n[1]$ shows that it contains $X_{n+1}$: rotate the triangle to place $X_n$ and $Z_n[1]$ at the ends, and use [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Therefore it contains $\bigoplus_nX_n$ and its shift. Put $P=\bigoplus_nX_n$. Writing the telescope triangle as $P\xrightarrow{a}P\xrightarrow{b}K\xrightarrow{c}P[1]$, its rotation is $P\xrightarrow{b}K\xrightarrow{c}P[1]\xrightarrow{-a[1]}P[1]$. Its end objects $P$ and $P[1]$ lie in $\mathcal L$, so the middle-object condition of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] gives $K\in\mathcal L$. As $K$ was arbitrary, every such $\mathcal L$ is all of $\mathcal T$. Taking their intersection, which is the definition of $\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathcal T}$ in the statement, proves the claimed equality.

Statement: 'finite admissible' is spelled out as a finite commutative ring killed by a power of ℓ, the convention of sk-thm-smooth-purity and of the sibling det-ctf-finite-comparison-localizing. The setting is k = algebraic closure of F_q with X of finite type, in the ordinary unbounded D(X_ét,A) of def-weil-pbc-derived-categories. Dctf means bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude. Loc is defined inline as the intersection of replete, coproduct-closed triangulated subcategories, correctly not cited as the pro-étale sk-def-localizing-closure. Nothing is weakened; dropping separatedness on X is a true strengthening. Step 1: the hypotheses of the detector lem-pur-etale-finite-ring-compact-generators hold (k algebraically closed, finite type, finite ℓ-primary ring). Its proof uses exactly the unit's family u_{s!}A_{U_s} over affine étale U_s, which detects through derived sections, so this is the unit's route reused rather than replaced. The detector itself already states compactness, so the extra citation of det-ctf-finite-compact-etale is redundant but harmless. Step 2: testing the zero map 0→K gives K≅0, and extending a nonzero map by zero on the other summands gives the weak generator of def-pc-generators. Step 3: every hypothesis of lem-pc-compact-generators-build-objects is met, and the triangles are taken from its statement only. Step 4: by induction, rotating Z_n→X_n→X_{n+1}→Z_n[1] and the telescope P→K→P[1] puts K in every such subcategory. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Edge cases: X empty, A=0, a point with F_ℓ, Z/ℓ² (only flat generators are used), unbounded K. A traversal of 16,567 nodes found no cycle; the missing def-weil-pbc-etale-morphism is pre-existing and outside this item. A duplicate search with rg found only pro-étale or module analogues, so same_as=[] is right. There are no SGA citations.
